summary: Six untracked gaps found, all with file:line evidence, none duplicating the three canonical backlogs. Most severe: the deterministic reassurance engine (the default drafter AND the safe floor under every LLM draft) still ships the literal garbled string 'as as' whenever a merchant bans the word 'soon' — the exact original sim bug, but the sprint's fix (llm-lint.ts word-boundary enforcement) only covers the LLM path, never the engine/floor path, and the eval harness's 57,614 assertions never catch it because they only check the banned word disappears, not that the resulting sentence still parses. Second: the onboarding wizard collects zero UI fields for campaignName/promisedWindow/baseline self-report despite complete backend plumbing (IntakeData fields, buildDefaultDisclosure, and a dedicated recordReportedBaseline function) — confirming the flagged claim exactly. Also found: backfillDisclosedEta and recordReportedBaseline are fully-built functions with zero callers anywhere in the repo; three API routes (gift-catalog, social-signal-feed, orders/timeline) duplicate logic that pages compute server-side directly and are never called; and the onboarding data-source picker tells merchants Gorgias/Zendesk ticket ingestion is 'coming soon' when ADR-0021 already shipped live webhook auth for both, contradicting the same wizard's own Connect-your-helpdesk step two clicks later.

gaps.gap: The deterministic reassurance engine — the DEFAULT drafter with no LLM key AND the safe floor under every LLM draft — still produces the exact garbled 'as as' text when a merchant bans 'soon', because its own hardcoded overdue phrase is run through a strip-and-collapse function with no post-check, and this path is never re-linted before shipping.
gaps.evidence: tideover/lib/engines/reassurance.ts:88-90 hardcodes "as soon as it's ready, and I'll update you the moment it moves" for overdue orders (the MODAL case per docs/TORCH-PASS-TO-OPUS.md — our ICP blew their window); line 99 runs it through stripBanned() (defined lines 59-66: \b<word>\b strip + whitespace collapse, no lint). tideover/lib/drafting/DeterministicDrafter.ts:8-17,26-39 confirms this engine is both the no-key default AND the floor under every LLM draft. tideover/lib/drafting/safe-floor.ts:164 (if decision.responsive return engine;) ships the engine's own text untouched for every WISMO/status ticket with zero re-lint. tideover/lib/drafting/llm-lint.ts:186-201 (bannedPhraseIn, word-boundary aware) is only invoked on the LLM path (line 220) and inside safe-floor's escalation-reply builder (safe-floor.ts:101-104) — never on the engine's own responsive output; llm-lint.ts:190 even names 'the bug in the engine's own stripBanned' but only for the punctuation-token case. tideover/evals/invariants.mjs:82-104 proves the strip executes using the customer's first name as bait, and lines 152-154 assert bannedSurvivor()===null against the SEEDED banned list — 'soon' is not in any seed fixture, so 57,614 assertions and 55 goldens never exercise this collision; the check only verifies the word disappears, not that the sentence still parses. This is the original sim finding (docs/sim-2026-07-12/TEN-CUSTOMER-SIMULATION.md:205, backlog item D1) but the fix only covers the LLM path.
gaps.tracked: NEW — OS8 (mission-control/tideover-hq.html:287) tracks a different, dormant punctuation-matching bug in the same function and is explicitly not this collision; TORCH-PASS-TO-OPUS.md §3 lists 'Banned phrases were prompt-only → Enforced post-generation, with word boundaries' as fixed, which is true only for the LLM path.
gaps.fix: Run the engine's merged draftText through llm-lint's bannedPhraseIn (or an equivalent block-not-mangle check) inside safeFloor before returning engine.text, and route any collision to the escalation reply instead of the strip.

gaps.gap: The onboarding wizard collects zero fields for campaignName, promisedWindow (the disclosed ETA the merchant told backers), or the four merchant-reported baseline numbers — despite full backend plumbing existing for all three. Confirms the flagged claim: backend-done, UI-missing.
gaps.evidence: tideover/lib/onboarding.ts:74,86 define IntakeData.campaignName? and .promisedWindow? as optional fields; lines 229-233 (buildDefaultDisclosure) and 383 (disclosedEtas: [buildDefaultDisclosure(intake)]) show the disclosed-ETA-at-onboarding feature is wired to read intake.promisedWindow. A full-file grep of tideover/app/onboarding/OnboardingWizard.tsx (1097 lines) for 'campaignName|promisedWindow|disclosedEta|baseline' returns zero matches, as does tideover/lib/onboarding-schema.ts and tideover/app/api/onboarding/route.ts. Separately, tideover/lib/baseline.ts:242-273 defines recordReportedBaseline(merchantId, {medianFrtSec, wismoPer100Orders, ticketsPerWeek, repeatWismoPct}) stamped source:'merchant-reported' — a repo-wide grep for callers outside its own definition returns nothing. Only the auto-measured half (captureCohortBaseline, called from lib/import.ts:361,386) is wired.
gaps.tracked: NEW — this is the exact item the audit brief flagged for verification; TORCH-PASS-TO-OPUS.md:183 claims baseline was 'given a write path at onboarding' but that's only true for the measured cohort, not the merchant-reported numbers, and none of the three lists mention the UI gap.
gaps.fix: Add a wizard step (or the post-import success screen) with the four baseline questions posting to recordReportedBaseline, and an optional 'what did you promise backers?' field feeding intake.promisedWindow/campaignName into the existing onboarding POST body and schema.

gaps.gap: backfillDisclosedEta() — the only mechanism to retroactively populate disclosedEta on orders imported before a merchant configured a disclosure — is fully implemented but has zero callers anywhere in the repo.
gaps.evidence: tideover/lib/import.ts:413-442 defines and exports backfillDisclosedEta(merchantId, merchantOverride?). grep -rn backfillDisclosedEta across the entire tideover tree returns exactly one hit — its own definition. No script in tideover/scripts calls it; none of the 29 routes under tideover/app/api call it.
gaps.tracked: NEW — not present in any of the three canonical backlogs; TORCH-PASS-TO-OPUS.md §8 calls disclosedEta 'the evidence pack's strongest exhibit' and notes it only works if populated, but the historical-backfill half is unreachable.
gaps.fix: Add a settings-page action or a one-time onboarding step that calls backfillDisclosedEta after the merchant sets their disclosedEtas config, so existing imported orders get stamped retroactively.

gaps.gap: Three fully-implemented API routes have zero callers anywhere in the app — the corresponding page components compute the same logic server-side directly instead, leaving the routes as orphaned, untested surface area.
gaps.evidence: tideover/app/api/gift-catalog/[customerId]/route.ts (47 lines, full recommendGift computation) — components/product/GiftSuggestion.tsx receives gift/reasoning/roi/availability as props with no fetch call, and its only render site, tideover/app/app/inbox/page.tsx:13,275, computes these server-side instead. tideover/app/api/social-signal-feed/route.ts (19 lines, calls scoreFeed) — its only consumer, tideover/app/app/social/page.tsx:1-36, is a server component importing scoreFeed and repos.social directly. tideover/app/api/orders/[orderId]/timeline/route.ts (14 lines, wraps computeTimeline) — a repo-wide grep for the path outside its own file returns nothing.
gaps.tracked: NEW — not on any of the three lists; EN1 (mission-control/tideover-hq.html) flags 'most routes have no error handling/trail' generically but does not name these as unreachable.
gaps.fix: Delete the three routes or wire a real caller (e.g. a client-side gift-suggestion refresh without a full page reload); either way they should not ship untested and uncalled.

gaps.gap: The onboarding wizard's data-source picker tells the merchant that Gorgias and Zendesk ticket ingestion is 'coming soon' (and omits Help Scout by name entirely), contradicting the live, working per-vendor webhook ingest (ADR-0021) exposed two steps later in the same wizard's 'Connect your helpdesk' panel.
gaps.evidence: tideover/components/product/DataSourcePicker.tsx:17-20 (comment: helpdesk sources shown greyed as 'Coming soon'), :40-45 (HELPDESK array lists gorgias, zendesk, intercom, tidio, all rendered live={false} at :227,238), :223,234 ('E-commerce — coming soon', 'Where do support tickets come from? — coming soon'). But tideover/lib/channel-adapters/ingest-vendors.ts:30 (IngestVendor = gorgias|zendesk|helpscout|generic) and :166-194 define real, live auth schemes (Bearer for Gorgias/Zendesk, HMAC-SHA1 for Help Scout), and tideover/app/onboarding/ConnectPanel.tsx:39,220 render a fully working credential UI for exactly those three vendors in the same wizard. Intercom/Tidio genuinely are stubs (IntercomAdapter.ts:25,30,66, TidioAdapter.ts:22,27 throw NotImplementedError) so the blanket label is correct for 2 of 4 entries, false for 2, and silent on the flagship one (Help Scout, INT1).
gaps.tracked: NEW — INT1 (mission-control/tideover-hq.html:253) tracks building Help Scout write-back, not this stale/self-contradicting UI copy in the read/ingest-side onboarding step; not mentioned in TORCH-PASS-TO-OPUS.md or the GTM doc.
gaps.fix: Move Gorgias/Zendesk/Help Scout out of the 'coming soon' group into a 'connects after setup' group (matching the component's own comment intent), name Help Scout explicitly, and keep only Intercom/Tidio/Shopify as genuinely 'coming soon'.
